coreReport:
Round 1 is finished in `calib.ts`, and in the fuzz every listed fault drops. Throttle inverted is now 0 of 3000 sessions in both harnesses, but 3-position switches are a trade: the middle no longer arms (54 → 4), and that adds 11 hard arm-polarity errors (details under "Could not do"). Tests (125/125) and typecheck pass, and the 12 000-run sweep is still 12 000/12 000.

**Starting point.** Because this is a retry, the working tree already held an earlier attempt's unreported changes to `calib.ts` and `calib.test.ts` (backup of the version before them: `.cache/v02/polish/base/`). I measured each of those rules, kept them all, and fixed two of its tests that could never pass: they jumped the stick from end to end in one frame, so it never passed the middle and the throttle was never assigned.

## Files changed
- **`C:/dev/ShramkoGSFPV/packages/input/src/calib.ts`**
  - **Throttle (kept):** holding the raw-low end, or the end it rested at during "let go", counts as "up" only after 2 s (`THROTTLE_DOUBT_HOLD_MS`). Pressing "Continue anyway" on "Throttle all the way down" while the stick sits still at the "up" end flips the direction.
  - **Throttle (new, `THR_LATE_MS` 1500, `THR_AWAY_STILL_MS` 300):** "down" is accepted after the normal 400 ms only if the stick first rested somewhere else on that screen for 300 ms. If it arrived in one movement that began before the screen, or was already down, it must stay 1.5 s. Mechanism, seeds slow:7 and bursty:141: the pilot's own push carried on into the "down" screen and silently confirmed an inverted push.
  - **Stir (kept):** "Continue anyway" always appears after 12 s. With fewer than four sticks found, every channel stays a candidate: unstirred channels are measured from their rest, ignored by the "held at its end" rule, and a side never explored is mirrored from the other side.
  - **3-position switch (kept):** if the switch reaches its far end after the middle was taken as ON, the far end becomes ON. New: this memory is cleared on Back.
  - **Arm OFF (kept):** if the switch is back at OFF before "Now flip it OFF" appears, the wizard waits for the next move.
  - **Arm OFF (new, `ARM_REACT_MS` 200, `ARM_SOON_WAIT_MS` 2000):** a return within 200 ms after that screen appears is treated the same way (seed armStartsOn:134, back ON after 180 ms). That case waits at most 2 s, so an instant robot is not stuck. A momentary button released within 200 ms after the screen becomes a toggle (seeds momentary:61 and 85).
- **`C:/dev/ShramkoGSFPV/packages/input/test/calib.test.ts`:** 4 new tests, the two broken tests fixed, and one older test moved to +300 ms so it still exercises the check-screen polarity swap.
- **Public API:** unchanged; `radio.ts` and `fakehid.ts` need nothing. `TUNING` gained the keys above and lost the unused `STIR_CONT_COVER`.

## Fuzz before → after
Mode 1 people following the Mode 2 drawing are left out (3000 sessions). First numbers are the core-fix harness, then `verify-fuzz`.

|---|---|---|
| Correct | 2756 → 2911 | 2749 → 2910 |

| 12 s with no hint or escape (97 sessions: stir.few 78, needFourAxes 11, coverage 8) | 97 → 0 | 97 → 0 |
| Throttle inverted | 79 → 0 | 79 → 0 |
| Momentary button taken as a level | 61 → 10 | 61 → 10 |
| Middle of a 3-position switch arms (minor) | 54 → 4 | 54 → 4 |

- Wrong answers caused by the simulated person (not the wizard) rose from 23 to 28. That is two wrongFirst sessions that used to hang and now finish with the person's own wrong stick.
- One new centre error, mode1:137, is a timing side effect: it passes with the doubt hold off and happens because a stalled tab counts as stillness, a problem the earlier verify already reported.

## How I checked it
- **Each rule has its own effect in the fuzz** (switching one rule off in a copy with flags):
  - throttle doubt hold off: inverted 0 → 1, throttle "down" hangs 4 → 14
  - Continue-flip off: inverted 0 → 7
  - 1.5 s late rule off: inverted 0 → 2
  - stir Continue-always off: 12 s silent 0 → 97
  - far-end rule off: middle arms 4 → 55, polarity 24 → 13
  - early-OFF wait off: polarity 24 → 50
  - momentary release rule off: momentary 10 → 57
  - 200 ms window off: momentary 10 → 22, polarity 24 → 26
- **Negative control for the tests:** removing each of 24 rules, one at a time, makes at least one test fail. The copy with nothing removed passes 37/37 (`python .cache/v02/polish/mutate.py`).
- **Negative control for the fuzz:** the baseline run shows every fault class above, so the harness can fail.
- **Sweep, run on a copy so `.cache/radio-ux` is untouched:** 12 000/12 000 correct; p50 27.2 s (was 26.5), p95 40.8 s (was 39.9), max 52.2 s. The first wizard as control is 95.2 % bad, so the control check passes.
- **Fake radio in Node (`.cache/radio-ux/robot-v2.ts`):** robot 100/100, the broken-stick control stays on the stir screen, human mode 40/40.
- **Static checks:**
  - `npx vitest run`: 10 files, 125/125 pass (37 in `calib.test.ts`).
  - `pnpm -r typecheck`: exit 0. The test files and the sim no-DOM config also typecheck clean, and `check-architecture` is ok.
  - Non-ASCII check: 0 characters in all my files.

## Could not do / still open
- **3-position trade-off:** the far-end rule adds 11 hard polarity errors. Careful simulated people look at the arm light 900 ms into their check flip while the switch sits in its middle detent, see OFF, and press Reverse. If the person looks after passing the detent instead, polarity is 11 either way and middle-arms is 2 vs 53. This needs the UI owner, for example showing "middle · disarmed" on the check screen.
- **Arm polarity, remaining 24:**
  - 13 are the 3-position trap above.
  - 2 are Reverse presses on a stalled tab showing an old screen.
  - 9 are switches that were already ON, where the person's own flip back ON came 200 ms or more after "Now flip it OFF" appeared. Only the check screen can catch those.
- **Momentary, remaining 10:** these are long presses released 300–400 ms after the screen appears. At that timing they look the same as a latching switch flipped OFF by a quick reader. A 250 or 300 ms window pushed latching-taken-as-momentary from 1 to 3 or 4, so I kept 200 ms.
- **Stir screen escape:** it is "Continue anyway"; "Pick the channel by hand" then appears on each stick screen after 8 s. A pick button directly on the stir screen would need UI work, because the channel list is empty outside a stick step.
- **Costs of the new waits:**
  - Throttle ends that read "up" at the raw-low end (gamepads, reversed throttles) need a 2 s hold instead of 0.7 s.
  - A throttle already down when the "down" screen appears waits 1.5 s instead of 0.4 s.
  - The instant fake-radio robot spends 2.5 s on "Now flip it OFF" instead of about 0.9 s.
  - A few slow people now take Continue and pick by hand: slow:19 went from 82 s to 131 s, while slow:81 went from a hang to correct.
- **Not addressed (outside Round 1):**
  - 19 reduced-travel sessions where the person never presses the offered Continue.
  - The stall-counts-as-stillness problem.
  - The ArmGate 100 ms "stale" rule, which would disarm a pad that only reports changes.
  - The wizard spec in docs, which is not my file.
- **Not measured on real hardware:** all new thresholds (200 ms, 2 s, 1.5 s, 300 ms) come from the person models, not a real radio or pad.

Scratch work, ablation tables, the mutation script and the fuzz results are in `C:/dev/ShramkoGSFPV/.cache/v02/polish/`. I made no git writes and started no servers.
